title: Molecular mechanisms underlying phenotypic overlap and AI-misclassification in rare bone diseases: Insights from SHOX-related signaling pathways in endochondral ossification.
authors: Fischer, Isabel; Bialdiga, Sina; Schmidt, Philipp; Bolmer, Eike; Javanmardi, Behnam; Mohnike, Klaus; Schanze, Denny
one_liner_zh: 该文探讨罕见骨病AI误分类与SHOX相关信号通路，虽涉及AI但核心为临床表型与信号通路综述，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或TF-DNA结合机制研究。
abstract: The diagnosis of rare bone diseases (RBDs) is challenged by their heterogeneity and rare occurrence. However, correct and timely diagnosis is highly relevant for the best therapeutic outcome of patients. We regarded two AI-approaches developed by the Bone2Gene project that aim to support the diagnostic process by assigning hand radiographs to RBDs. We noticed a predominant misclassification of several RBDs into the group of SHOX-related short stature. To find potential genetic explanations for this overlap, we performed a literature research for SHOX-related signaling in endochondral ossification and connections to the signaling underlying other RBDs. We found that SHOX activates the expression of the structural protein aggrecan (ACAN) and represses FGFR3-induced RAS/RAF/MAPK signaling, displaying signaling connections to ACAN-related growth disorder as well as Hypochondroplasia and Achondroplasia, respectively. Additionally, we conclude that the high phenotypic variety of SHOX-related short stature also contributes to the misclassification of RBDs that do not show a direct connection to SHOX-related signaling. Overall, we deepened our understanding of the occurrence of misclassification in both Bone2Gene approaches. Complemented with genetic testing, Bone2Gene can be a valuable tool in the diagnostic process of RBDs.
abstract_zh: 罕见骨病（RBDs）的诊断因其异质性和罕见性而面临挑战。然而，正确及时的诊断对患者的最佳治疗结果至关重要。我们关注了Bone2Gene项目开发的两种AI方法，旨在通过将手部X光片归类至RBDs来支持诊断过程。我们注意到几种RBDs被主要错误分类至SHOX相关矮小症组。为寻找这种重叠的潜在遗传学解释，我们对软骨内骨化中SHOX相关信号传导及其与其他RBDs信号传导的联系进行了文献研究。我们发现SHOX激活结构蛋白聚集蛋白聚糖（ACAN）的表达，并抑制FGFR3诱导的RAS/RAF/MAPK信号传导，分别显示出与ACAN相关生长障碍以及软骨发育不全和软骨发育不良症的信号联系。此外，我们得出结论，SHOX相关矮小症的高表型变异性也导致了对未显示与SHOX相关信号传导直接联系的RBDs的错误分类。总体而言，我们加深了对Bone2Gene两种方法中错误分类发生情况的理解。结合基因检测，Bone2Gene可成为RBDs诊断过程中的宝贵工具。
